notes: ROBOTS: https://www.bloomingville.com/robots.txt fetched FIRST, before any other request on the host (HTTP 200, 68 bytes, profile safari17_2_ios). Quoted IN FULL, it is three lines: 'User-agent: *' / 'Disallow: /Files/Papirkurv/' / 'Disallow: /*?cartcmd=*'. There is NO Claude agent anywhere in it - no ClaudeBot, no anthropic-ai, no Claude-Web, no Content-Signal - and no Crawl-delay and no Sitemap directive. Neither disallowed pattern was requested: nothing under /Files/ was touched, and the only query string used anywhere was the site's own '?GroupID=&PageNum=N' pagination, which contains no cartcmd. ACCESS: clean. probe.fetch() returned HTTP 200 on the first or second fingerprint every time (chrome131, safari18_0_ios, safari17_0); no bot wall, no challenge, no 403, no 429. 2s per-host pacing left in force. TREE: taken from Bloomingville's OWN A-Z category index at https://www.bloomingville.com/en/products/category, which is the site's own complete category tree (the mega-menu dropdowns are injected client-side and expose only the 11 departments - Category, Series, Tableware, Kitchen, Accessories, Kids, Outdoor, Furniture, Lighting, Christmas, New products - so I did NOT stop at the menu, exactly as BATCH_BRIEF s5 warns). https://www.bloomingville.com/sitemap.xml exists but is a 281-byte stub containing only /redirect/redirect, and /en/sitemap.xml and /sitemap_index.xml both 404, so the A-Z index IS the authoritative tree. THE BATH DEPARTMENT: grepping the EN A-Z index for /en/products/bath and /en/products/bed-bath returns exactly six nodes and no more - all-for-bed-bath, a-mix-of-this-and-that, cosmetic-bags, dispensers-tumblers, jewelry-stands-boxes, towels - plus the alias entry 'All for the bathroom' -> /en/products/category/bed-bath. I cross-checked the DANISH A-Z at https://www.bloomingville.com/da/produkter/kategori in case the English site suppressed a local node: it exposes five (/da/produkter/badevaerelse/alt-til-sovevaerelse-bad, /badevaerelse/haandklaeder, /badevaerelse/saebedispensere-krus, /sovevaerelse-bad/diverse, /sovevaerelse-bad/smykkestativer-smykkeskrin) - a strict SUBSET of the English six, so EN is the superset and nothing is hidden. The Danish labels are worth recording because they disambiguate two English names: 'Sæbedispensere & krus' = the recorded Dispensers & Tumblers node, and 'Badeværelsestilbehør' (literally 'bathroom accessories') is the node whose English label is the vaguer 'Various for bedroom & bathroom' / H1 'Diverse'. There is no bath, shower, enclosure, tap, basin, toilet, bidet, vanity, bathroom cabinet, towel rail or toilet-roll holder node anywhere on the site in either language. WHY THE RECORDED LEAF IS BATHROOM (rules 13, 23, 24): 'Dispensers & Tumblers' is a bath-department child at the deepest available level, self-canonical, with its own product grid. Its 2 products are Bea Soap Dispenser Set (Nature, Stoneware) and Aurora Tumbler (Blue, Stoneware) - a soap dispenser and a bathroom tumbler, both named explicitly in rule 13, and ceramic/stoneware which rule 22 does not exclude. The DA label 'Sæbedispensere & krus' confirms the intent. QTY SOURCE AND PROOF - THIS SITE PRINTS NO TOTAL, AND ITS JSON-LD IS UNSAFE: Bloomingville renders no 'N products' string on any PLP (probe.counts_in() surfaces nothing usable). Each PLP DOES carry a CollectionPage JSON-LD whose mainEntity is an ItemList, but I tested it and it is BADLY WRONG - for /bath/towels it reports 1,141 itemListElements against a grid of exactly 1 product; for /category/baskets it reports 42 against a grid of 30; for /category/hooks-coat-racks 24 against 20; for /bed-bath 10 against 5; and on /bath/dispensers-tumblers, /bath/jewelry-stands-boxes, /category/bags and /category/mirrors it emits no ItemList at all. It is therefore NOT used for any figure here. Every count in this record comes from ENUMERATION TO EXHAUSTION of the rendered grid (rule 26's fallback), page size 12, walking ?GroupID=&PageNum=N until a page returns no product tile not already seen: Towels 1 (1 page), Dispensers & Tumblers 2 (1), Diverse 5 (1), All for the bathroom 5 (1), Jewelry Stands & Boxes 8 (1), Bags 13 (2: 12+1), Mirrors 17 (2: 12+5), Hooks & Coat racks 20 (2: 12+8), Baskets 30 (3: 12+12+6, page 4 empty). Unique product handles were collected from the tiles' own /varekort/<handle> hrefs, so duplicates across pages cannot inflate a figure. The results discriminate fully per node (1, 2, 5, 5, 8, 13, 17, 20, 30 - no constant, no round cap) and every page's H1 matched the node requested. Nothing is estimated, no parent figure is reused for a child, and nothing is summed across siblings. DEDUP: already_extracted() run on every candidate leaf, every review node and every rel=canonical target. One hard hit - /en/products/category/mirrors (Final.xlsx 'Mirrors'), banked in review[]. The recorded leaf returns None. Locale blind spots (b) and (c) checked explicitly rather than assumed: the recorded page's own hreflang block lists five alternates, ALL on www.bloomingville.com - da /da/produkter/badevaerelse/saebedispensere-krus, fr /fr/produit/salle-de-bain/distributeurs-de-savon-et-gobelets, de /de/produkte/badezimmer/seifenspender-becher, and en/x-default on the recorded URL - and already_extracted() returns None for every one of them, so there is no cross-host or cross-locale alias hiding in the index. Bloomingville runs no separate country domain. Blind spot (a) was also live here and was caught: /en/products/bath/cosmetic-bags and /en/products/category/bed-bath and /en/products/bath/all-for-bed-bath are canonical ALIASES of /category/bags and /products/bed-bath respectively, and were collapsed to one record each under rule 28. EXCLUDED AND WHY: Category > Hooks & Coat racks (20) inspected in full and excluded - Chalix/Ferri/Lester/Lewi/Cella hooks and Mille/Blu/Mallen/Oswall/Padova/Ross coat racks, i.e. hallway coat hardware, with no towel rail, towel ring or robe hook and no bathroom parent, so rule 17 does not reach it. Category > Baskets (30) and Category > Storage inspected and excluded as general storage (rules 12, 31/33) - water-hyacinth, seagrass, rattan and polyrattan baskets w/lid; the one laundry basket (Mios) carries no bathroom designation. Category > Rugs & Doormats, Category > Textiles, Living room > Cushions/Throws (rule 20 Textile). Category > Trays, Jars w/lids, Bowls & trays for decoration, Vases, Candles, Candle holders, Decoration, Wall decoration, Illustrations, Pedestals (rule 21 Decor - most already in Final.xlsx). Lighting and its 5 children (rule 19, all already in Final.xlsx). Furniture and its children (Furniture.xlsx). Kitchen and Tableware (Kitchen & Dining, already in Final.xlsx). Room scents / Scent diffusers (personal-care and home fragrance, not bathroom fittings). Christmas, Easter, Offers, Outlet, Must-haves, Spot items, News, Series (rule 25 promotional). CONCLUSION: Bloomingville does operate a small bath department, and its one genuine bathroom leaf - Dispensers & Tumblers, 2 products - is recorded. Its four sibling nodes are a textile (routed), a jewellery-box node, a canonical alias of the general Bags node, and an overlapping roll-up, all banked in review[] with their exact counts and URLs so nothing is silently skipped, along with the two roll-up-only residue products. This is NOT a robots exclusion and NOT an access block - robots.txt names no Claude agent and every request returned HTTP 200.
